title: Asia Week New York announces exceptional 2027 dealer roster
summary: The Asia Week New York Association announced an all-star roster for its highly anticipated 2027 edition. Featuring 21 renowned international galleries, including two online exhibitions, 26 museums and six major auction houses–Bonhams. Christie’s, Doyle, Freeman’s, Heritage Auctions, and Sotheby’s–this vibrant celebration of Asian art and culture will run from March 11th through March 19th. “As we head into our 18th year, Asia Week New York remains the singular destination for collectors, curators and art enthusiasts from all over the world,” says Margi Gristina, the Asia Week New York chairperson. “With an exceptional line-up of gallery exhibitions, auction sales, and special events throughout the city, the 2027 edition promises to be as enticing as ever.” The only event of its kind in the United States, Asia Week New York shines a spotlight

title: Morphy's December auctions feature Tiffany lamps, rare Coca-Cola prototype, and $10,000 note
summary: Morphy’s Fine & Decorative Arts auction slated for December 1-2 is brimming with premium-quality holiday gift ideas. Featured items include not one but two Tiffany Studios leaded-glass floor lamps, a lovely platinum emerald-cut diamond line necklace, a 1915 Coca-Cola Root Glass experimental prototype bottle, and a 19th-century carved wood cigar store Indian figure of Metamora that stands 84 inches tall. This exciting two-day auction features an exceptional array of fine jewelry, luxury watches and sterling silver, alongside fine art, antiques, and decorative collectibles – more than 1,200 top-quality lots in all – with gift ideas for even the most selective recipients on your holiday list. title: Detroit Institute of Arts celebrates one-year anniversary of its reimagined African American art galleries
summary: One year after opening its reimagined African American art galleries, the Detroit Institute of Arts (DIA) today announced a $1 million gift from Larry D. and Brenda A. Thompson, supporting the future of the museum’s celebration and presentation of African American art. In recognition of the gift, one of the four galleries will be named the Larry and Brenda Thompson and Family Gallery, and the galleries will feature several paintings on loan from their personal collection. The anniversary also marks the launch of a new audio tour and companion podcast, bringing Detroit voices into the galleries while expanding the visitor experience. Since opening last October, the galleries have become a cherished part of the DIA experience, welcoming more than 250,000 visitors. title: Researchers solve 200-year archaeological puzzle of the Parthenon's east pediment in Frankfurt
summary: A 2,500-year-old image is taking shape once more: much like a giant three-dimensional jigsaw puzzle, years of research have finally succeeded in reassembling the fragments of one of the most famous works of antiquity and piecing them together to form a complete picture. From 18 November 2026, the Liebieghaus Skulpturensammlung will present, for the first time, an archaeologically grounded proposal for the complete reconstruction of the Parthenon’s east pediment in the exhibition “Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle”. To this end, the research team led by Vinzenz Brinkmann, Head of the Liebieghaus Department of Antiquities, has re-examined around sixty surviving fragments using 3D scans, assigned them to individual figures and cross-referenced them with ancient written sources as well as Roman reproductions of lost Greek sculptures. title: The Frick Collection presents Alison Watt's first solo US museum exhibition in spring 2027
summary: Starting in spring 2027, The Frick Collection will present an exhibition celebrating an artistic dialogue across centuries: between the contemporary British painter Alison Watt (b. 1965) and the seventeenth-century Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. Watt has created a suite of seven still-life paintings in her acclaimed intimate realist style, taking inspiration from Van Dyck’s portraits of his fellow painter Frans Snyders and Snyders’s wife, Margareta de Vos—two highlights of the Frick’s renowned collection of Old Master paintings. Through these works, she explores themes of visual memory, identity, and portraiture, as well as the processes and mysteries of the act of painting. Imagined Lives: Alison Watt at the Frick will debut the series in the Frick’s Cabinet Gallery, marking Watt’s first solo museum show in the United States. title: Hamburger Kunsthalle and Centre Pompidou present landmark new media art exhibition
summary: Bringing together some of the most radical voices from the past three decades, the exhibition UNSTABLE MEDIA IN THE 21ST CENTURY presents around 40 landmark works from Centre Pompidou’s New Media collection. The uncertain fate of emerging technologies has always challenged the standards of continuity and permanence expected of a museum collection. And yet these technologies have shaped our sensory memory and become sedimented within us over time, even forming what might be likened to a second skin. Their impermanence is equalled only by the long-term resonance they imprint upon perception, the imagination, and the constant reworking of knowledge. UNSTABLE MEDIA IN THE 21ST CENTURY invites

title: Mattatuck Museum presents first museum solo exhibition of reclusive painter Franne Davids
summary: The Mattatuck Museum presents Franne Davids and the World She Painted, on view through February 14, 2027. Organized by Chief Curator Rebecca McNamara, the exhibition introduces audiences to the hypnotically colorful figurative paintings by Waterbury native Franne Davids in her first museum solo exhibition. Davids (1950–2022) spent much of her adult life painting in the basement of the home she shared with her parents. There, living with schizophrenia, she created more than 400 paintings, many featuring feminine figures she referred to as “girls” or “ladies.” These figures became imaginary companions within her otherwise-reclusive world. title: Huis Marseille presents a premiere of Adolphe de Meyer's rediscovered collection of photographs of Venice
summary: The Substance of a Venetian Dream is the first ever European museum exhibition devoted to the photographer Adolphe de Meyer (1868–1946). This follows the remarkable discovery in 2019 in the municipal library of Tours: a series of 75 photographs documenting his life and photographic work in Venice. This collection is being displayed in its entirety for the first time, and offers an exceptional glimpse into his personal and artistic world. Adolphe de Meyer was born in Paris in 1868 and enjoyed a fascinating and ground-breaking career in both Europe and the United States. Historians recognise him today principally as a pictorialist photographer (a movement that approached photography as an art form), as a virtuoso portraitist, and above all as a fashion photographer. title: Expanded Marina Abramović survey arrives in Rome following Venice Biennale presentation
summary: The Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea presents Marina Abramović: Historical Works and Transforming Energy, an exhibition marking the artist’s 80th birthday that brings together some of the most significant historical works of her career alongside a selection of Transitory Objects. Spanning different phases of her artistic practice, the exhibition explores the relationship between the performative dimension of the body and the slower, more profound temporality of matter. Following its presentation at the Gallerie dell’Accademia in Venice on the occasion of the 61st International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia, the exhibition arrives in Rome in an expanded version. Curated by Shai Baitel, Artistic Director of the Modern Art Museum (MAM) in Shanghai, in close collaboration with the artist, the exhibition situates Transforming Energy within the broader evolution of Marina Abramović’s artistic practice. title: Tania Franco Klein named Deutsche Bank's 2027 "Artist of the Year"
summary: Deutsche Bank has named Tania Franco Klein its Artist of the Year for 2027. To mark the start of her tenure, Franco Klein will present her work in Deutsche Bank’s VIP lounge at Frieze Los Angeles from February 25 to 28, 2027. This is the first time the bank has tied the award so closely to its role as Global Lead Partner of the Frieze art fairs. Born in 1990, the Mexican artist and photographer stages psychologically charged portraits, interiors, and landscapes filled with cinematic tension. “My world is psychological, emotional, and intimate,” says Franco Klein. “I’m not trying to tell a story.” Through color and intuitive lighting, she translates emotional states into physical spaces. Her compositions are shaped by a keen sense of spatial staging, which she developed while studying architecture. title: Frist Art Museum presents exhibition of Jewish ceremonial objects
summary: The Frist Art Museum presents Beauty and Ritual: Judaica from the Jewish Museum, New York, an exhibition that explores the artistic, cultural, and ritualistic significance of more than 130 Jewish ceremonial objects (Judaica) spanning six continents and nearly four thousand years. Drawn from the world-renowned collection of the Jewish Museum in New York City, Beauty and Ritual s on view in the Frist’s Upper-Level Galleries from October 30, 2026, through February 7, 2027. title: Anawana Haloba selected to create Tate Modern's Infinities Commission in 2027
summary: Tate Modern today announces Anawana Haloba as the third artist to undertake the Infinities Commission, the annual commission to showcase the limitless experimentation of contemporary art. Each year, an expert panel selects a pioneering international artist to create a major new work for the Tanks, Tate Modern’s unique spaces for performance, installation and time-based media. Haloba’s commission will be unveiled in June 2027. Anawana Haloba (b.1978, Livingstone, Zambia) creates immersive installations that draw on voice, sound and storytelling to explore memory, resistance and collective experience. Working across sculpture, video and performance, she examines the ways histories are remembered, shared and reimagined. Rooted in oral traditions, music and ritual, her works bring together voices from across generations and geographies, creating spaces for reflection, solidarity and exchange. title: Jim Lambie debuts new paintings, sculptures, and neon work at Sadie Coles HQ
summary: The material language of Jim Lambie finds its expression in the electric collision between found objects and prismatic colours, transforming ordinary items into charged totemistic works of art. For his seventh solo exhibition with Sadie Coles HQ, Lambie is showing a new series of paintings and sculptures at the Bury Street gallery. In a sequence of five paintings, gaffer-tape and printed elements combine in a new series of formalist, polyphonic canvases, informed by sound, rhythm and imbued with disruptive tension. New sculptures bring together performative objects that reference the body: talismanic leather gloves encrusted with buttons intervene with angular, skeletal sculptures of a modernist tradition made from crushed metal barriers. Within this complex dramaturgy of registers and forms, entangled metals seem to writhe, collapse, and expand. Threading through both floors of the gallery will be a site-responsive neon work. title: Lotus L. Kang wins Sobey Art Award grand prize
summary: The National Gallery of Canada (NGC) and the Sobey Art Foundation (SAF) are pleased to announce that Lotus L. Kang has been awarded the 2026 Sobey Art Award, Canada's most established prize in contemporary visual arts. The artist receives the award's CAD 100,000 top prize. Marking its 23rd edition this year, the Sobey Art Award celebrates artists who are at a critical juncture in their careers. The winner was announced at a special celebration at the NGC, livestreamed to audiences across the country. The other five shortlisted artists—Melaw Nakehk'o (Circumpolar), Samuel Roy-Bois (Pacific), Audie Murray (Prairies), Caroline Monnet (Quebec) and Shane Perley-Dutcher (Atlantic)—each receive CAD 25,000, while the 24 longlisted artists each receive 10,000, bringing the total value of the award to 465,000. title: Feriarte brings together some of the most celebrated names in modern and contemporary art
summary: From 21 to 29 November, Feriarte 2026, organised by IFEMA MADRID, will once again make Madrid an unmissable meeting place for collectors, industry professionals, and art lovers. With around 80 galleries and antiques dealers taking part, the fair will present a carefully curated selection spanning the major artistic movements of the 20th and 21st centuries. It offers a rare opportunity to discover—and acquire—works by some of the most celebrated names in modern and contemporary art. As it looks ahead to its 50th anniversary, Feriarte reaffirms its commitment to excellence, authenticity, and the quality of the works on display. The 2026 edition will bring together works by such pivotal artists as Pablo Picasso, Joan Miró, Salvador Dalí, Joaquín Sorolla, Eduardo Chillida, Jorge Oteiza, Antoni Tàpies, Jaume Plensa, Juan Genovés, Antonio López, Antonio Saura, Luis Feito, Fernando Botero, and Yayoi Kusama—an exceptional offering for established collectors and first-time buyers

title: O'Hare breaks ground on new Concourse E and offers first look at its design
summary: The City of Chicago and Chicago Department of Aviation (CDA) broke ground on The New Concourse E at O’Hare International Airport today. Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) in collaboration with Ross Barney Architects, Juan Gabriel Moreno Architects (JGMA), and Arup, the new building comprises the next phase of ORDNext, the largest terminal expansion in O’Hare’s history. The New Concourse E will introduce approximately 315,000 square feet of new passenger space and add new gates to O’Hare, while creating a more intuitive and comfortable travel experience. As the second satellite concourse designed by the SOM-led team, the building extends the architectural language of The New Concourse D, adapting its expressive structural system, natural materials, and light-filled public spaces for domestic operations.

title: PIASA and Harper's Bazaar Interieurs partner for landmark auction in Paris
summary: To celebrate its recent move to its new space at 54, rue de Monceau in Paris, the auction house PIASA has teamed up with the editorial team of Harper's Bazaar Intérieurs to orchestrate a landmark auction titled "Le Design Bazaar," taking place on Wednesday, November 25. This unprecedented event offers a snapshot of the current zeitgeist and the major movements of the 20th and 21st centuries. Through a dialogue between historical pieces, design icons, and contemporary creations, the sale brings together over 170 carefully curated lots. title: New Museum announces partnership with The Vega Foundation to produce new video works
summary: The New Museum today announced a multi-year partnership with The Vega Foundation enabling the annual production of a major new video work. Furthering both organizations’ commitment to supporting the creation of new productions by the most exciting artists working today, the partnership will be inaugurated in February 2027 at the New Museum in New York City with the presentation of a new video installation created by artist Korakrit Arunanondchai. In keeping with The Vega Foundation’s mandate to bring the artistic projects it supports to audiences in Canada, Vega will also curate a solo exhibition of Arunanondchai’s work including this new co-commission at a Canadian institution. title: Christie's opens first Exhibition in Asia dedicated to Modern South Asian art
summary: Christie's presents its first exhibition in Asia dedicated to modern South Asian Art, 'Masterpieces of Modern South Asian Art: Highlights from the Dabriwala Collection', which also marks one of the first public exhibitions of the Dabriwala Collection. Free and open to the public from 18 – 29 November at The Henderson, Christie's Asia Pacific headquarters in Hong Kong, the exhibition brings together over twenty works by leading modern artists from South Asia, offering a rare opportunity to explore the major movements and developments that have shaped the category over the 20th century through one of its most significant private collections. Spanning multiple generations of collecting, the exhibition reflects the vision and stewardship of Surbhit Dabriwala and his family in building a collection of exceptional depth and significance. title: Benaki Museum marks Cahiers d'Art centenary with exhibition
summary: On the occasion of the centenary programme of Cahiers d’Art, which unfolds across a constellation of major institutions including the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice, MDAM–Collection Zervos in Vézelay, LUMA Arles, Musée national Picasso-Paris, the Museum of Modern Art in New York, and Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía in Madrid, the Benaki Museum presents an exhibition, curated by Polina Kosmadaki and Vassiliki Dannil, that brings the history of the legendary Parisian journal into direct encounter with one of the richest, most multifaceted, and vast museum collections in Greece. The exhibition brings Cahiers d’Art back into the geographical and cultural horizon from which Zervos himself emerged, while placing his project in dialogue with the encyclopedic and cosmopolitan formation of the Benaki Museum
